name: Automation Intelligence & Quality Profiles
changes: Release-pipeline recovery hotfix: v3.6.82 carries the complete v3.6.81 Automation Intelligence & Quality Profiles runtime forward unchanged while restoring the canonical Source commit trigger format.
Monitored TV metadata now refreshes on schedule even when Continuous Automation/download grabbing is disabled, keeping future episodes and Calendar data current independently of unattended downloads.

Quality upgrade decisions now distinguish generic WEB from explicit WEB-DL and treat dynamic range as a real upgrade dimension: HDR upgrades SDR, Dolby Vision upgrades HDR, and Dolby Vision with HDR/HDR10/HDR10+ fallback is the preferred terminal dynamic-range state.
Release parsing preserves independent Dolby Vision, HDR10+, HDR10 and HDR flags so combined DV + HDR fallback releases are represented correctly instead of collapsing to one mutually exclusive label.
Automatic selection, Interactive Search, Smart Import no-downgrade checks, automatic-grab preflight and cutoff/Wanted decisions share the same source/dynamic-range upgrade model.

Replaces the primitive free-form New Quality Profile editor with a structured builder: templates, ordered quality ladder, cutoff, HDR/Dolby Vision, codec, audio, PROPER/REPACK, size, preferred groups, reject terms and advanced custom scoring rules.
Corrects stale third-party notice text to SABnzbd 5.1.2/current NewzDeck wording without changing the pinned SAB runtime.
Preserves the accepted Newsgroup Browser performance architecture, SABnzbd 5.1.2 integration, download/post-processing pipeline, Metadata Server v0.3.3 and Diagnostic Collector v1.0.31.
regression_guards: v3.6.82 proves server, Automation, SAB adapter, browser JavaScript and Quality Profile Builder CSS normalize exactly to the accepted v3.6.81 runtime after removing release identity only.
The guarded publisher must write the canonical release trigger as Source commit: <40-hex-source-sha>; the workflow parser remains fail-closed.

v3.6.81 tests explicit WEB-DL > generic WEB at equal resolution, SDR -> HDR -> Dolby Vision -> Dolby Vision + HDR upgrade progression, and prevents dynamic range from overriding a lower base resolution tier.
The structured Quality Profile Builder must expose canonical quality tiers plus Allow/Prefer/Require/Avoid trait policies and preserve advanced custom scoring rules.
The service loop must call monitored metadata refresh independently of the automatic-grab enable switch.
The v3.6.80 final UX/accessibility stylesheet remains an exact protected prefix; v3.6.81 adds only the reviewed Quality Profile Builder suffix.
The v3.6.78 LF/Linux yEnc source and accepted helper hash gates remain unchanged, along with frozen browser admission/sampling/header/resolver constants and SABnzbd 5.1.2.
